appraisal_events.evidence: With Swann's carriage already waiting for Odette, Mme Verdurin announces she is taking Odette home herself, in the little seat beside M. de Forcheville; Odette simply answers 'Oui, Madame,' and Swann, caught off guard with the door already open and seconds counted, can only blurt out his confusion.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin publicly and abruptly displaces Swann, reassigning Odette's ride to Forcheville in front of the group, a direct, witnessed exclusion at the moment Swann most expected to have Odette to himself.

status_effects.explanation: Swann is shut out of the intimate space of Odette's ride home, publicly and abruptly, after having assumed it as his due.
Swann is left desperate and out of control, unable to hide his distress and unable to bear returning home without Odette, exposing his dependency in front of the group.
Mme Verdurin publicly grants Forcheville the seat beside Odette in Swann's place, a witnessed mark of favor that visibly elevates him over Swann in that moment.
